reuse.why: All affected consumers reuse the existing recurrence conversion and weekend helpers, although occurrence filtering and adjustment remain composed separately.

duplication.why: Holiday recognition and movement are shared, but upcoming-date and range handlers repeat the dropped-occurrence filtering and adjusted-day projection.

placement.why: Most scheduling policy stays in shared/schedules.ts, but holiday-dependent search margins introduce scheduling policy into the server handler.

scope.why: The changes are confined to the requested scheduling features, their consumers, configuration types, and relevant tests.

maintainability.why: Consumers must coordinate separate enumeration, dropping, and adjustment helpers while maintaining different search-window strategies, making future scheduling changes harder to own.

bypasses_abstraction.where: The changed consumers call applyWeekendRule or applyWeekendRuleToDay and the shared isDroppedWeekendOccurrence predicate.

disguised_duplication.where: The repeated filtering and adjusted-day projection in getUpcomingDates and getDatesInRange are direct repetition rather than disguised implementations.

abstraction_drift.where: WeekendRule gains daily and holidays; applyWeekendRule adds a daily exemption, and getWeekendRuleTake adds a daily-specific enumeration branch, while changed consumers continue using shared helpers.
